body.estimand_functional: \(\widetilde C_N=\{b\in\mathcal B:N\widehat\gamma_N^{-1}d_{H_N}(m_N-b\mathbf1,\{a q_N(r):a\in\mathbb R,\ r\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\})^2\le\overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\}\), where \(\overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\) is a certified outward \(N^{-1}\)-approximation to the supremum, over the legal physical set \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\), of the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2\).

sampling_model.design: Deterministic quasi-uniform triangular arrays in a fixed bounded Lipschitz domain in \(d\in\{1,2\}\), with \(h_N\asymp N^{-1/d}\) and separation comparable to \(h_N\).
sampling_model.units: The observed units are sites \(s_{i,N}\); uncertainty comes from one centered stationary bivariate Gaussian-field realization evaluated at those sites.
sampling_model.treatment: The continuous exposure is \(X(s_{i,N})\), and the homogeneous conditional slope in \(Y(s)=\beta X(s)+W(s)\) is the target.
sampling_model.overlap: No exposure nugget or nonspatial variation is assumed; identification comes from the smoother signed cross-tail with \(p\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\subset(1/2,1)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the marginal microergodic scale ratio \(\gamma=c_W/c_X\) is estimated by residual quadratic variations; \(p\), \(A\), and the nonmicroergodic ranges are profiled or bounded over their stipulated compact sets.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: High-frequency dissipation of exposure--confounder coherence supplies sufficient identification and motivates spectral adjustment.
Relative local smoothness conditions characterize consistent slope estimability and local differences or Laplacians yield consistent estimators.
Locally preconditioned inversion-free covariance estimators are root-\(N\) consistent and asymptotically normal on multidimensional irregular lattices.
Higher-order quadratic variations consistently estimate Mat\'ern smoothness and microergodic parameters on three structured irregular-design families.
Appropriately filtered smoothed spatial cross-periodograms on lattices are relatively consistent and asymptotically normal.
The scalar Mat\'ern microergodic parameter has root-\(N\) Gaussian behavior uniformly over a compact nuisance range with known smoothness.
Conditional quasi-likelihood-ratio tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without restrictions on identification strength.
A plurality-rule aggregate mode consistently estimates the spatial slope, and valid candidate slopes are asymptotically normal.

body.tldr: High-frequency separation can identify a spatial slope even without nugget variation, but existing theory does not justify confidence intervals when the signed cross-tail shrinks to zero and its exponent disappears. Three exact affine-annihilating local slopes generate a finite-dimensional mean cone \(\beta\mathbf 1+B_Nq_N(p)\) whose secants and tangents remain uniformly separated from the slope direction. The central theorem derives the corresponding Gaussian experiment and feasible scale studentization on the actual quasi-uniform design, yielding uniformly honest root-\(N\) confidence sets and root-\(N\) risk through every \(A_N\to0\); a complete-data Gaussian lower bound matches both rates. Exact attainable least-favorable calibration, beyond conservative chi-square coverage, is the explicit open question.

project_justification.gap: Published spatial-confounding results identify or consistently estimate slopes under local spectral separation, and published fixed-domain results deliver Gaussian inference for scalar covariance combinations. They do not provide design-uniform slope inference when the observation-scale cross-tail is local to zero and its exponent is unidentified.
project_justification.niche: The exact Mat\'ern-one-half, no-nugget model isolates a nonregular but finite-dimensional nuisance geometry in which three scales separate \(\beta\) uniformly, while affine filters make arbitrary quasi-uniform designs analytically tractable in dimensions one and two.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the actual-design Gaussian experiment, residual-scale studentization, conservative uniform coverage, root-\(N\) diameter and risk, and matching honest lower bounds, while exposing attainable exact calibration as a sharply delimited open theorem.

body.related_work: Guan, Page, Reich, Ventrucci and Yang motivate the problem by showing that decay of high-frequency exposure--confounder coherence can identify a spatial slope; their spectral construction informs the observation-scale tail parameter used here. Datta and Stein characterize consistent infill estimability and construct local-difference and Laplacian estimators over broad Gaussian-field classes; their result informs the local-filter architecture, while the present target is uniform inference on a narrower signed-cross-tail class. Keshavarz, Nguyen and Scott obtain root-\(N\) Gaussian covariance estimation from preconditioned quadratic forms on irregular lattices, and Loh, Sun and Wen develop higher-order variations on selected irregular designs; both inform the finite-matrix proof. Lim and Stein prove normality of filtered cross-periodograms on lattices and inform the cross-form covariance analysis. Zhang and Li establish the scalar Mat\'ern microergodic geometry and root-\(N\) inference over range nuisance, respectively. Andrews and Mikusheva inform calibration under weak identification but do not supply the spatial experiment. Burman, Ogburn and Datta provide the conditional PM2.5 and COVID-19 consumer and a distinct plurality-based identifying model.
body.technical_internal_limitation: First differences are insufficient in \(d=2\): the analytic covariance remainder creates an \(O(h_N)\) slope bias and normalized correlations of order \(1/r\) create a logarithmic variance factor. Exact affine annihilation removes the quadratic covariance term and yields summable fourth-difference dependence. Three-scale profile intervals may nevertheless have large constants when \(p_{\min}\) is close to \(1/2\); the proposal claims rate optimality, not an efficient constant.
body.honest_scope: The conservative chi-square confidence theorem, root-\(N\) risk and length bounds, and rate lower bound are the principal claims to prove. Equality of the least-favorable coverage envelope and certified attainable quantiles remain open in Open-ended Question 1. The scope excludes nuggets, unknown marginal smoothness, nonstationarity, independent Fourier-coordinate approximations, and covariance classes broader than the stated signed bivariate Mat\'ern family. The PM2.5 and COVID-19 use is conditional on empirical Mat\'ern and quasi-uniform-design diagnostics and does not itself establish a nonparametric causal estimand.
